# 1 Enoch Chapter 46 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS | **Section:** Book of Parables

---

**46:1** There I saw the One called the Head of Days. His hair was white as wool. Beside him stood another figure — his face was human in appearance, and his countenance radiated grace, like the face of one of the holy angels.

**46:2** I asked my angelic guide, who had been showing me all these hidden things, about this Son of Man — who he was, where he had come from, and why he was standing beside the Head of Days.

**46:3** He answered me: "This is the Son of Man, the one in whom righteousness lives, with whom righteousness makes its home. He is the revealer of all hidden treasures, for the Lord of Spirits has chosen him, and his standing before the Lord of Spirits surpasses everything else in righteousness, now and forever."

**46:4** "This Son of Man you have seen will overthrow kings and the powerful from their thrones, and will break the grip of the strong and shatter the teeth of sinners."

**46:5** "He will topple kings from their thrones and their kingdoms, because they refused to praise and honor him, and refused to acknowledge gratefully the one from whom their power was given."

**46:6** "He will humiliate the powerful and fill them with shame. Darkness will be their home, and worms their bed. They will have no hope of rising from that bed, because they refused to honor the name of the Lord of Spirits."

**46:7** "These are the ones who set themselves up as judges over the stars of heaven, who raise their fists at the Most High, who dominate the earth. Everything they do is marked by injustice. Their power comes from their wealth, and the gods they trust in are idols of their own making — all while they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits."

**46:8** "They are the persecutors of his holy communities and of the faithful who hold fast to the name of the Lord of Spirits."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Chapter 46 is the watershed of the entire Enochic corpus. The vision of the Son of Man beside the Ancient of Days is the most direct interpretation of Dan 7:9–14 in all of Second Temple literature. This chapter and the chapters immediately following (47–49) shaped the New Testament's use of "Son of Man" more profoundly than any other non-canonical text.*
